publication_endpoint: independent comparative test of temporal microhabitat complementarity as a buffer of broad-scale residency
core_hypothesis: temporally complementary hydrological microhabitats allow animals to track suitable states internally and retain broad-scale residency

primary_estimands.A_ht: fraction of familiar area currently within usable hydrological/microhabitat state
primary_estimands.Async: asynchrony among microhabitat suitability time series
primary_estimands.broad_relocation: movement or home-range displacement beyond the familiar area

primary_predictions: fine-scale microhabitat use tracks current hydrological state while broad home-range position remains stable
higher HPI reduces broad relocation at equal mean habitat quality
relocation rises nonlinearly when retained suitable area falls below a threshold
hydrological specialists gain more from high HPI than broad-niche species
temporal complementarity predicts residency better than static heterogeneity
falsification: mean habitat quality performs as well as temporal complementarity
internal microhabitat switching does not increase with hydrological change
heterogeneous portfolios do not reduce broad relocation
niche breadth does not modify portfolio benefit

northern Gulf Coast multi-species wetland-bird data
